rows.label: Five Italian-track courses of 3+ credits each: Italian IV, ITAL 2900 or 2204, and three more ITAL courses at the 2202 level or above
rows.note: The board counts only ITAL courses numbered 2202 (the required Italian IV) or above, fixed at 3 or more credits. Electives from other departments, and half courses (1.5 or 2 credits), are not counted here: confirm them in the rows below. At most two of the five may be transfer or exam credit.

limits.label: Taken at another institution or by exam credit

rows.label: If an elective comes from another department (Romance Studies, History, Government ...), confirm it counts as a course in Italian Studies
rows.note: The page does not list the non-ITAL courses that count, so the board cannot place them: confirm with the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rows.label: A 1.5- or 2-credit ITAL course is only half a course; two such courses must be combined to make one
rows.note: The board leaves half courses and variable-credit ITAL courses out of the count; confirm any pair you rely on.

rows.label: At least one of the electives is taught in Italian (literature/culture)
rows.note: The board cannot see the language of instruction.

rows.label: Cap of two of the five courses that may come from study abroad or another school
rows.note: The board caps transfer and exam credit at two courses; courses taken abroad through Cornell are not visible to it, so confirm those count toward the same two.

rows.label: At most one of the five courses taken S/U; every other course completed with a B- or better
Declare the minor by registering your intent with the Director of Undergraduate Studies
